tutorialPage.architecture.body: The repository currently consists of backend services, the enterprise console, and the chat app. The enterprise app handles configuration, the chat app handles usage, and the backend runs conversations, knowledge, tools, and tasks.
tutorialPage.architecture.layer.configur: Models, employees, knowledge bases, skills, SOPs, tools, and scheduled tasks define what an employee can do.
Knowledge citations, long-term memory, session state, and feedback become input to the next decision.
tutorialPage.architecture.layer.entry.bo: The chat app accepts real user phrasing, while the enterprise app handles configuration, operations, and review.
tutorialPage.architecture.layer.observab: Trace, event logs, and feedback analysis make every execution trackable and improvable.
Router, Agent Loop, Skill Runtime, and Response Generator advance the task.
tutorialPage.architecture.title: Architecture overview
tutorialPage.development.body: One principle during feature work: configuration changes must be verifiable in runtime, and runtime failures must be explainable through trace.
tutorialPage.development.title: Development guide
tutorialPage.faq.body: Most issues can be located in one of six layers: model, knowledge, SOP, tools, permissions, and trace.
tutorialPage.faq.item.knowledge.answer: Check the document parsing state, whether the knowledge base is bound to the current employee, and whether the question covers key concepts from the documents.
tutorialPage.faq.item.knowledge.question: Why are there no citations from the knowledge base?
tutorialPage.faq.item.model.answer: Check the API key, whether Base URL includes `/v1`, the model ID, account balance, and network connectivity. Get the default model test passing before validating the chat app.
tutorialPage.faq.item.model.question: What should I do when model tests fail?
tutorialPage.faq.item.sop.answer: Check the node instruction, expected_user_info, and slot extraction strategy so already satisfied information is skipped.
tutorialPage.faq.item.sop.question: Why does the SOP repeat questions?
tutorialPage.faq.item.tool.answer: Check the SOP node allowed_actions, tool enabled state, parameter schema, and whether the tool is bound to the current employee.
tutorialPage.faq.item.tool.question: Why was the tool not invoked?
tutorialPage.faq.title: Common troubleshooting
tutorialPage.features.body: PilotDeck groups capabilities into WorkSpace, Router, Memory, Always On, and Gateway. StaffDeck maps that pattern to enterprise digital employees, with emphasis on role boundaries, knowledge governance, workflow execution, tool usage, and operational review.
tutorialPage.features.item.employees.bod: Each employee maintains its own role description, service scope, resource bindings, and operations history, which makes it suitable to separate support, shopping guidance, operations, and knowledge-assistant roles.
tutorialPage.features.item.knowledge.bod: Policies, product content, delivery notes, and service wording are parsed into searchable chunks, while replies keep citation clues to reduce answers that sound right but cannot be verified.
tutorialPage.features.item.memory.body: User preferences, project background, review conclusions, and collaboration habits are retained as searchable records so later sessions can inherit verified context.
tutorialPage.features.item.memory.title: Memory
tutorialPage.features.item.schedules.bod: Employees can run prompts one time, daily, weekly, or monthly, which fits inspections, weekly reports, reminders, exception follow-up, and recurring analysis.
tutorialPage.features.item.skills.body: Browser actions, queries, document handling, MCP, or project workflows can be packaged as skills so multiple employees can reuse and iterate on them.
tutorialPage.features.item.skills.title: Skills
tutorialPage.features.item.sops.body: Workflows are described through nodes, required information, allowed actions, interruption strategies, and response rules. Already satisfied information is not repeatedly requested.
tutorialPage.features.item.sops.subtitle: Process constraints
tutorialPage.features.item.sops.title: SOPs
tutorialPage.features.item.tools.body: HTTP tools and built-in tools connect orders, products, knowledge retrieval, or internal services so employees can query, validate, create, and trigger actions.
tutorialPage.features.item.tools.title: Tools
tutorialPage.features.item.trace.body: Conversation logs, trace, feedback analysis, and event records connect routing, tool usage, replies, and improvement clues so failures can be traced to a specific step.
tutorialPage.features.item.trace.title: Tracking and feedback
tutorialPage.features.title: The core features are not isolated points but one employee runtime system
tutorialPage.flow.body: From the user message to the final reply, every step in the middle should leave evidence in logs and trace.
tutorialPage.flow.code:

tutorialPage.intro.body: The core of StaffDeck is not just chatting. It gives each real-world role its own configuration, resources, execution rules, and operating history. Every employee can have independent knowledge, SOPs, tools, and memory, and every conversation can be reviewed through routing, tool calls, replies, and feedback.

tutorialPage.intro.painPoint.tools: Tool invocation is hard to control

tutorialPage.quickStart.body: This is not a one-off demo. It is the shortest operating loop: configure, verify, review, and retain.
Prepare an OpenAI-compatible model, the single-port service, and demo tenant data so the enterprise app, chat app, and API docs all run from one local entry point.
The system starts, pages open, and the model is ready to generate.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.knowledge.b: Turn business documents into a knowledge base, then break key workflows into nodes, required inputs, allowed actions, and response rules.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.knowledge.o: The employee follows business rules instead of improvising.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.review.body: Use trace, feedback, memory, and scheduled tasks to retain failure causes, stable wording, and long-term tasks.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.review.outc: One test run becomes input for the next configuration improvement.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.role.body: Pick a low-risk but workflow-heavy role first, such as after-sales support, shopping guidance, operations monitoring, or an internal knowledge assistant.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.role.outcom: The role boundary is clear, including what it can and cannot handle.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.role.title: Define one real role
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.testing.bod: Do not limit testing to ideal prompts. Use real user phrasing that covers missing info, complete info, corrections, interruptions, and human handoff.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.testing.out: The flow skips already satisfied inputs and asks for confirmation before critical actions.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.tools.body: Give each employee only the tools it truly needs, such as order lookup, purchase flows, internal queries, or knowledge search.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.tools.outco: Tool calls are verifiable and both inputs and outputs can be reviewed.
tutorialPage.quickStart.step.tools.title: Connect only the necessary tools
tutorialPage.quickStart.title: From an empty system to one reviewable employee
tutorialPage.reference.body: These are not navigation shortcuts but the objects and acceptance criteria that should be checked during configuration.
tutorialPage.reference.item.employees: Employees: clear role boundaries, explicit resource bindings, and manageable states.
tutorialPage.reference.item.knowledge: Knowledge: document parsing completed, citations are hit, and wording can be reviewed.
tutorialPage.reference.item.models: Models: one default model, successful connection tests, and masked key display.
tutorialPage.reference.item.operations: Operations: logs, trace, feedback, and memory form a closed loop.
tutorialPage.reference.item.sops: SOPs: nodes, slots, allowed actions, and response rules are explicit.
tutorialPage.reference.item.tools: Tools: parameter schemas are verifiable and test calls return results.
tutorialPage.reference.title: Configuration reference
tutorialPage.runtime.body: StaffDeck conversations are not single-turn Q&A. They form a traceable execution chain across routing, knowledge, skills, SOPs, tools, and response generation.
tutorialPage.runtime.title: How one business request is advanced
tutorialPage.showcase.body: Start with low-risk, workflow-dense, reviewable tasks before gradually connecting stronger tools and higher-risk actions.
tutorialPage.showcase.item.afterSales.bo: Refund, return, and exchange workflows need order confirmation, eligibility checks, cause collection, and controlled promises, which makes them ideal for validating SOPs and tool calls.
tutorialPage.showcase.item.afterSales.st: After-sales SOP -> Order lookup tool -> Risk response rules -> Trace review
tutorialPage.showcase.item.knowledgeAssi: Turn policies, delivery documents, and service standards into knowledge bases, then continuously refine wording through citations and feedback.
Knowledge base -> Citation-backed replies -> Feedback analysis -> Knowledge updates
tutorialPage.showcase.item.operations.bo: Recurring inspections, weekly reports, exception reminders, and follow-up tasks can be configured as scheduled tasks so the employee keeps working in the background.
tutorialPage.showcase.item.operations.st: Scheduled tasks -> Execution records -> Memory retention -> Next-run reuse
tutorialPage.showcase.item.shopping.body: Use product knowledge, comparison skills, and purchase tools to complete recommendations, price explanations, purchase confirmation, and outcome feedback.
tutorialPage.showcase.item.shopping.stac: Product knowledge -> Comparison skills -> Purchase SOP -> Tool result feedback
tutorialPage.showcase.title: Enterprise scenarios worth testing first
